project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas Juglans microcarpa reference module
project_scope.note: Built as the companion family to the existing Fagaceae oak module.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the long alternate pinnately compound leaf, then confirm male catkins and a nut enclosed by a husk.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Unisexual; male flowers commonly in catkins, female flowers in short terminal clusters.
family_diagnostics.fruit: One-seeded nut enclosed by a fleshy or fibrous outer husk.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Confirm alternate compound leaves plus a husked nut. Split the genera with fruit and twig pith: Carya usually has a sutured splitting husk and solid pith; Juglans an indehiscent husk and chambered pith. Catkins alone are not diagnostic.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Little walnut becomes easy when you pair the long compound leaf with the husked nut and stop using catkins alone.

steps.title: 1 · See the Texas Hill Country form
steps.look_for: A woody plant with long odd-pinnately compound leaves and many narrow leaflets.

steps.title: 2 · Inspect twig and buds
steps.look_for: Walnut-type twig/bud architecture; chambered pith is a useful secondary character when visible.

steps.title: 3 · Learn the catkin context
steps.look_for: Slender male catkins on older wood.
steps.why_it_matters: Useful supporting evidence, but not enough by itself because oaks also have catkins.

steps.title: 4 · Finish with the husked nut
steps.look_for: A small globose fruit with an outer husk surrounding a hard nut.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the decisive local Juglandaceae fruit pattern.

comparisons.title: Juglandaceae vs Fagaceae
comparisons.rule: Walnuts have pinnately compound leaves + husked nuts; local oaks have simple leaves + acorns in cupules.

comparisons.title: Catkins are not enough
comparisons.rule: Both walnuts and oaks make male catkins, so always combine them with leaf and fruit architecture.

visual_lesson.caveat: Use aroma only from naturally handled foliage; do not damage plants solely for an odor test.
